learning_outcomes.text: Applies the fundamentals of materials science, technology, and chemistry. Applies environmental technologies and sustainability. Understands the relationship between microstructure, synthesis or processing, and material properties.
Applies quality criteria in the selection, reception, and control of materials.

Predicts the material's structure and behavior from the composition of metallic alloys. Establishes relationships between material properties and their structure. Knows the treatments a material can undergo to modify its behavior. Selects the most suitable materials for each application and their required state of use.
Becomes aware of the importance of material selection, design, and recycling.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Engineering Materials: Description of the different types of materials used in engineering.
Chemical bonding in materials: Types of chemical bonds in the different materials. Correlation with material properties.
Perfect Crystalline Structure: Bravais lattices. Lattice parameters. Crystalline structure in metals and ceramics.
Defects in crystalline structure: Diffusion in solids. Point defects in crystalline structure. Diffusion and activation energy. Applications in surface carburization.

Phase diagrams and microstructural evolution: Phase rule. Types of binary systems (with total and partial miscibility). Eutectic, eutectoid, and peritectic systems. Fe-C diagram. Lever rule. Evolution of the microstructure during cooling.
Kinetics and heat treatments: Kinetics of phase transformations. TTT (time/temperature/transformation) diagrams. Heat treatments.
Metals and alloys. Mechanical properties: Types of alloys. Steels and cast irons. Dislocations and higher-order defects. Mechanical properties of metals.
Ceramics and glasses: Types of ceramic materials. Glasses. Applications and mechanical properties.
Polymers: Concept and structure of polymers. Applications.

assessment_rules: Mandatory attendance for laboratory practices is required, and a minimum grade of 5 is needed in the practice block to pass the course. A minimum grade of 4/10 is also required for the second partial exam. In the resit (second call), the grades for practices and problems (30%) are retained, and a comprehensive written exam will cover the remaining 70% of the grade. Any fraudulent use of tools in evaluative activities will result in a failing grade for that specific activity.
